newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian admits fighting tourist, not murder.
newsitem.headline: Australian admits fighting tourist, not murder.

text.p: The Australian man charged with the brutal murder of British tourist Brian Hagland at Bondi Beach admits fighting with the 28-year-old Londoner, his lawyer told a court on Thursday.
But lawyer Leigh Johnson said her client, Aaron Martin, 22, would plead not guilty to murdering Hagland on September 7.
"He admits he had a fight with the deceased," Johnson said during a bail hearing for Martin in the New South Wales Supreme Court, which Martin watched via a video link from his prison.
Johnson asked for bail on the provision Martin stayed at home, pointing out that he voluntarily surrendered to police.
"You also have to consider that jails are not safe places and they are not safe places for young men," Johnson told reporters outside the court.
"There are a number of people who have gone into jail and literally contracted AIDS in jail...and I don't want him to be one of them," Johnson said.
Johnson said the case may take 18 months to go to trial, but prosecutors have said they would have the case ready in a month.
Prosecutor Chris Maxwell opposed bail, arguing that Martin would be a risk to the community if released.
"(He is) a young man who seems to have an attraction to beating people up in public places, who seems to have an attraction to violence and brutal violence," he told the court.
Supreme Court Judge Vince Bruce will decide on the bail application on Friday.
Sean Cushman, 22, has been charged with being an accessory to Hagland's murder and has been granted bail. Both Martin and Cushman are due to appear in court on November 1.
Hagland died from head and internal injuries after he was assaulted in a street attack witnessed by his fiancee in the early hours of Saturday, September 7.
His fiancee, Connie Casey, 25, has said two men kicked and punched Hagland to death in an unprovoked attack near Australia's best known beach.
